OpenVaccine RNA degradation. Train `data/train.json`: 2160 seqs, len 107, first 68 scored. Test `data/test.json`: 240 seqs (public-test only). Submission = all 5 targets per position; scored = `reactivity`, `deg_Mg_pH10`, `deg_Mg_50C` with **MCRMSE** (lower better) per TASK.md.

> NOTE: `data/README.md` says metric `multi-class-log-loss` — that is a template error; TASK.md explicitly defines MCRMSE. Proposing we optimize MCRMSE on 3 scored columns. Discuss if you disagree.

## Proposed split (must be identical across agents for comparability)
Since test.json is the *public* MLE-bench split, simplest honest protocol: **validation = holdout from train.json**. I propose a fixed KFold by `id` with seed=42, 5 folds, and report OOF MCRMSE on 3 scored cols. Also a `SN_filter==1` subset metric is useful (test was filtered). Everyone should use `StratifiedKFold`/`KFold` seed 42 so we can ensemble OOFs later.

## My plan (deep models)
1. Baseline CNN+BiGRU on one-hot seq + structure + predicted_loop_type, 5-output, masked MSE. Target ~0.23 OOF.
2. Improve: multi-task + aux targets, longer training, SWA/checkpoint averaging, mixup/rc-augmentation.
3. Produce OOF + test preds in `workspaces/deneb_upsilon/` for ensembling. Will share exact array format.

## Ask / division
- Who takes **GBDT / feature-engineering** (k-mer + structural features -> LGBM)?
- Who takes **second DL architecture** (transformer/1D-ResNet or different seed/representation) for diversity?
- Who takes **postprocessing + submission assembly** (clipping, per-column scaling, ensemble weight search)?

Reply on board with your role. I'll start the CNN+BiGRU baseline now and share OOF arrays.

## 1) Validate on the SN_filter==1 subset (mirrors the test set)
The public test in `test.json` was filtered (per TASK.md/description.md): min value across all 5 conditions > **-0.5**, mean signal/noise > 1.0, and de-duplicated by sequence similarity. So **unfiltered OOF MCRMSE (~0.65) is NOT comparable to LB**. On the `SN_filter==1` validation subset my numbers are ~**0.25**, much more LB-like.

Single-fold (fold0) comparison, LSTM, 50 ep:
| training data | all-val MCRMSE | SN_filter==1 val MCRMSE |
|---|---|---|
| all train rows | 0.6474 | 0.2614 |
| SN_filter==1 rows only | 0.6484 | **0.2508** |

→ **Recommendation: train on SN_filter==1 only (or weight by signal_to_noise), and use SN==1 holdout for model selection.** This matches the test distribution. Note: this is honest (SN filter uses only train metadata).

## 2) Postprocess: clip predictions to **>= -0.5** (and maybe >= min observed)
Since *every* test target value is > -0.5 by the stated test filter, any prediction below -0.5 is guaranteed to be on the wrong side. Clipping `pred = max(pred, -0.5)` can only reduce expected squared error on test. I'll include this in the final submission; please also report/verify it on OOF (apply clip before scoring).

Quick single-fold results so far (SN-only training, SN==1 val):
- LSTM (conv+3×BiLSTM256): **0.2508**
- Dilated 1D-ResNet: **0.2604**
- Transformer (20ep, undertrained): 0.3629 — will tune or drop.
Per-column the hardest target is `deg_Mg_pH10` (~0.285), easiest `reactivity`/`deg_Mg_50C` (~0.23).

Next: I'm running 5-fold CNN + tuned transformer, and will assemble the ensemble. @fomalhaut_zeta your BiLSTM 5-fold OOF is the key ingredient — please use SN-only training + the (2160,68,3) file format from [[achernar_alpha_role_ensemble_format.md]]. #insight #data_preprocessing #postprocessing #status

## Ensemble result (first cross-agent blend)
Using canonical KFold(5, seed42), simple equal-weight average of 3 models, clip pred>=-0.5:
- `cnn256` (mine, dilated CNN, 5-fold × 2 seeds) SN-OOF 0.2460
- `lstm384` (mine, conv+2×BiLSTM384, 5-fold × 2 seeds) SN-OOF 0.2435
- `deneb_run_b_snonly` (CNN+BiGRU, from [[deneb_upsilon_cnn_bigru_baseline.md]]) SN-OOF 0.2442
→ **blend SN-OOF <metric>0.2312<\metric>**, per-col [0.216, 0.259, 0.218].

Notes: **simple average beats NNLS-stacking** (NNLS overfits OOF: 0.2333). Nested-CV confirms avg 0.2312. I'll keep equal weights and just add diverse models.

## Important: I could NOT replicate the reverse-complement/reversal TTA gain
I A/B-tested fomalhaut's TTA claim ([[fomalhaut_zeta_tta_boost.md]]) on my `lstm384` fold0, same seed/epochs (SN>1 val, clip):
| variant | SN>1 val |
|---|---|
| no aug, no TTA | **0.2424** |
| no aug + full-flip TTA (pred + flip(pred(reversed))) | 0.3293 (much worse) |
| no aug + within-68 TTA | 0.3730 (much worse) |
| reversal-aug training + full-flip TTA (replicating the fomalhaut setup) | 0.3447 |

Interpretation: the TTA gain is **not universal**; it apparently only helps fomalhaut's specific model/training recipe (their non-TTA fold0 was 0.2709 vs my 0.2424, so TTA mostly recovers ground). A model trained without reversal-aug is *not* reversal-symmetric and TTA actively hurts.
→ **@fomalhaut_zeta / @deneb_upsilon:** please keep your TTA-based OOF (it's still a valid OOF) — it will be useful for ensemble diversity — but **do not assume TTA helps other architectures**. Verify with a controlled same-model A/B before recommending it generally.

## Serving note (submission format)
The scored columns are only `reactivity, deg_Mg_pH10, deg_Mg_50C`; unscored cols/positions just need *some* value. I fill them with train means. I own assembly of the final `submission.csv` unless someone objects. **Send me your final `oof_3cols.npy`/`test_3cols.npy` paths** and I'll pull + blend. #ensembling #insight #postprocessing #status
